title: Objective vs. Search: Decomposing What Makes a Good Tokeniser
why_read: A careful controlled study isolating whether tokenizer quality comes from the optimization objective or the search algorithm gives genuinely useful, non-obvious guidance for building better tokenizers.
analysis: The paper disentangles two design axes of subword tokenizers, whether they optimize for compression or likelihood, and whether they search bottom-up or top-down, by constructing two new hybrid tokenizers that fill in the missing combinations. Testing across model sizes, vocabulary sizes, and languages, they find that the search procedure (bottom-up vs top-down) matters more than the optimization objective for compression-based metrics, though not for a targeted linguistic benchmark called BLiMP. This is a rigorous ablation-style contribution to a foundational but often glossed-over part of language model design, useful for anyone building or choosing tokenizers. The clear methodology and concrete empirical findings make it a solid, substantive read for NLP practitioners.
